title: Wrong Way On Purpose
mood: cheeky, grown and sweet on her
subject: a husband who turns left when the whole Friday line dance at the Elks Lodge turns right, so that for one count of eight he is facing his wife of thirty years
caption: Modern Southern soul in the drum-machine line-dance style of the Black Southern club circuit. A programmed drum-machine shuffle with stacked handclaps on two and four; a warm synth bass walking the two-step groove; keyboard horn stabs and short organ chords answering each line; a bluesy electric lead guitar filling the gaps with bent notes. Warm, close and plain, the drums and voice forward, the keys in the middle. Male voice, a gritty conversational baritone, a grown storyteller who talks the dance-step cues and sings the hook while a crowd answers him. 96 BPM, B-flat major. Cheeky, grown and sweet on her. No vintage live horn section or 1960s Stax-style live band, no gospel choir, no country twang, no zydeco accordion, no trap drums, no autotune.
lyrics:
[Intro - drum-machine shuffle, handclaps and an organ stab]

[Verse 1]
Friday night at the Elks Lodge, DJ Ray calls the slide
Forty of us in four straight lines on the hardwood floor
Thirty years my baby's been dancing on my left
Brings her good shoes in a grocery bag and dances in her flats

[Pre-Chorus]
Quarter-turn, the whole room swings to the right
And I go left

[Chorus]
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)
Whole room's looking at the wall and I'm looking at you
Eight counts face to face, then I fall back in line
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)

[Verse 2]
Little man at the front says Mister, you messing up the line
His grandmama says hush, he been doing that since ninety-six
My wife rolls her eyes like she ain't been waiting all week
Then she winks at me on the count of eight

[Spoken - dance cues]
Now slide to the right, now bring it on back
Everybody turn... well, almost everybody

[Chorus]
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)
Whole room's looking at the wall and I'm looking at you
Thirty years and I still ain't learned it right
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)

[Outro - organ, handclaps and a guitar fill]
Last song, that little man turns left too
And his grandmama hollers Lord, it's catching
